proposed_from.topic: Construct finite-sample replacement-DP honest confidence intervals for the pointwise Hölder CATE at an interior anchor under overlap, bounded common-support outcomes, and positive local design density. On the concrete uniform-design attainable subclass, build a fully private higher-order local learner with privatized nuisance pilots and localized linear and quadratic moments; prove an unrestricted-finite-rank remainder bound, a transcript-wise nonempty clipped interval, and an optimized expected-length upper phase separating privacy-free, ordinary private-regression, and higher-order global-sensitivity terms. On the unchanged full class, prove the ordinary γ-smooth honest-length lower bound and the fixed-dimensional β-smooth private direct-regression upper bound, and state the resulting nonsharp full-class and attainable-class brackets, including a public selector between the two attainable upper constructions. Keep the exact full-class nuisance/private-Gram confidence frontier open; no matched full-class phase is claimed.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest private causal interval result, SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025, concerns a root-\(n\) population ATE and adds privatization uncertainty to an influence-function variance. The closest private CATE result, SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025, provides point learners and quasi-oracle conditions without intervals. The proposed contribution is different in mathematical object and proof route: a finite-sample honest interval for a nonregular pointwise Hölder CATE whose radius exposes higher-order nuisance bias and localized quadratic sampling error, with a replacement-private composition proof and an optimized expected-length upper phase. ShohamEtAl2026 does not subsume this claim because its black-box resampling theorem is asymptotic and does not derive the uniform KBRW-class bias or phase-sensitive length. No exact full-class lower phase is claimed.

seed_details.anchor: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024, Theorems 1--2 and Sections 3.1--4.4; AcharyaSunZhang2021, Theorems 1 and 3
seed_details.kernel: Derive one two-sided replacement-private minimax theorem with the privacy-free fuzzy and regression terms and the competing \(q\)-private and \(\gamma\)-private terms.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the support-hole product-mixture Hellinger calculation by a positive paired-cell expected-Hamming coupling, then privatize every term of the attaining higher-order learner.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor Introduction frames CATE as a regression and functional hybrid; Definition 1 places zero density on bump transitions; Proposition 1 makes the one-record prior averages equal; Theorem 2 attains the nonprivate rate only under nonprivate pilot and Gram conditions. AcharyaSunZhang2021 requires a coupling cost as an input rather than deriving it.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for central private pointwise nonparametric regression and private CATE minimax theory located only the distributed pointwise theorem of CaiChakrabortyVuursteen2024 and quasi-oracle private CATE results, not this target-method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 plus private Assouad because one can insert their Hellinger bound into a private test.
seed_details.rebuttal: Private Assouad needs expected record-Hamming transport, and the published witness violates the positive local-density band through support holes.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the explicit phase rate \(r_n\), and both converse and fully private attainment are present.
seed_details.burned_reason: The paired-microcell q<gamma angle is incompatible with gamma-Hölder CATE smoothness; its invalid transport step is not revived.

seed_details.anchor: AcharyaSunZhang2021, Theorem 3 and Lemma 15; KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024, Lemma 2 and Proposition 1
seed_details.kernel: Prove a reusable approximate-private testing theorem for paired prior mixtures with exact one-record cancellation and a low product-mixture Hamming transport cost.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple occupancy counts and posterior cell signs before coupling records, rather than independently coupling two ordinary product laws.
seed_details.opened_evidence: AcharyaSunZhang2021 Lemma 15 scans and changes records under an ordinary discrete-law coupling; the CATE anchor instead integrates over one shared latent sign per microcell, so posterior dependence is the missing step.
seed_details.destination_search: CaiWangZhang2023ScoreAttack and KamathMouzakisSinghal2022 supply tracing and approximate-private leakage tools, but neither treats paired causal mixtures with equal one-record marginals.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a restatement of private Le Cam with a different coupling.
seed_details.rebuttal: Constructing a low-Hamming coupling when one-record marginals agree but product mixtures differ through shared latent signs is the theorem, not an assumed input.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is uniform over a class of paired mixtures and has a pointwise CATE corollary, not a single tuned witness.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Redo the conditional bias and variance decomposition after privatizing nuisance pilots, local basis moments, the Gram matrix and inverse, and the degenerate quadratic correction.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The KBRW estimator uses independent pilots and a localized inverse Gram; Sheffet's positive-definite release treats fixed-dimensional second moments, so shrinking bandwidth and growing basis dimension are not covered.
seed_details.destination_search: SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025 privatizes nuisance and target stages, but its Theorem 2 gives quasi-oracle conditions for ordinary orthogonal learners rather than the low-smoothness higher-order rate.

seed_details.rebuttal: The quadratic correction and local inverse have bandwidth- and dimension-dependent sensitivity, and naive composition yields a distinct private-Gram rate.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names an explicit estimator and rate envelope rather than merely applying privacy to an existing algorithm.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize when an ordinary positive-density two-point CATE perturbation can yield a privacy branch below the \(\gamma\)-regression barrier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lower-bound the one-record total variation by the local mass times CATE separation before applying private Le Cam.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Private Le Cam converts ordinary product-law total variation into expected Hamming distance, and the distributed regression paper's pointwise construction follows this ordinary bump geometry.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel is bounded by four threads. First, KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 Theorems 1--2 give the privacy-free pointwise CATE frontier; Definition 1 and Proposition 1 show exact prior cancellation, while Remarks 4--6 and Appendix B.1 reveal that the construction places zero covariate mass on bump transitions. Kennedy2023 Theorem 1 and its Discussion develop the first-order and local-polynomial precursors and identify the then-open minimax question. RobinsLiTchetgenVanDerVaart2008 Sections 2--3 provide the higher-order influence-function and degenerate \(U\)-statistic method that the upper bound adapts. Second, AcharyaSunZhang2021 Theorems 1 and 3 convert a supplied expected-Hamming coupling into private Le Cam or Assouad risk; Lemma 15 illustrates record scanning for ordinary product laws. KamathMouzakisSinghal2022 Theorem 3.5 and CaiWangZhang2023ScoreAttack provide adjacent approximate-private tracing arguments, but both require score or exponential-family structure absent from a causal fuzzy prior mixture. Third, SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025 Theorem 2 proves quasi-oracle private orthogonal CATE learning and Appendix A.2 names privacy-induced causal uncertainty as unresolved; NiuEtAl2022 Theorem 6 and its Discussion provide a private composition meta-algorithm and request privacy-accuracy theory. Neither states Hölder pointwise minimax rates. Fourth, CaiChakrabortyVuursteen2024 Theorem 2.1 and its pointwise upper and lower results provide the nearest \(\gamma\)-smooth regression benchmark, but for heterogeneous distributed privacy rather than one central curator. Sheffet2019 Algorithms 1--3 and Theorem 3.2 provide positive-definite private second-moment releases only in fixed-dimensional linear regression. Searches through September 8, 2026 found no closer public theorem combining central replacement privacy, pointwise CATE, positive local density, paired fuzzy cancellation, and fully private higher-order attainment.
